title: Zigzag Conversion
summary: Develop a function that converts a given string into a zigzag pattern across a specified number of rows and then reads the string by lines.
statement: Develop a function that converts a given string into a zigzag pattern across a specified number of rows and then reads the string by lines. The function should be named convert and accept a string s and an integer numRows as parameters.
constraints: 1–1000 characters: uppercase/lowercase English letters, commas, or periods.
1 <= num_rows <= 1000. Write characters down the rows then diagonally upward repeatedly; read rows from top to bottom.
hints: Only each character's destination row matters; a full visual grid is unnecessary.
Append to row buckets while changing direction at the top and bottom rows.
For each character, append it, set direction at a boundary, and move the row pointer; join all row buckets at the end.
One row, or at least as many rows as characters, leaves the input unchanged.
editorial: Simulate the current row and travel direction. Every character goes into exactly one row bucket. Reverse direction at the first and last row, then concatenate buckets in reading order. The reference uses lists to avoid repeated immutable-string concatenation. The oracle instead computes the triangular-wave row index using the cycle length 2(rows−1), then orders characters by row and original position.

tests.explanation: The rows contain PAHN, APLSIIG, and YIR; joining them gives PAHNAPLSIIGYIR.
The four rows read PIN, ALSIG, YAHR, and PI, giving PINALSIGYAHRPI.
